stories.headline: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
stories.summary: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded.
stories.why_it_matters: Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test.
Technical Implementation: AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts.

Deployment & Impact: And while safety depends on monitoring, monitoring requires observability : the capacity to capture what the system did, process it into signals, and present those to humans or automated oversight systems.

stories.headline: The FDA wants to pull its approval of a drug. It’s not so easy.
stories.summary: In May 2021, the US Food and Drug Administration released a lengthy briefing document on an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis that often damages the kidneys and lungs. The agency was on the fence about whether to approve the treatment, and it wanted an independent advisory committee to weigh in.
stories.why_it_matters: Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies? Participants in the study, which had been conducted by the California biotechnology company ChemoCentryx, did appear to have slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies? Participants in the study, which had been conducted by the California biotechnology company ChemoCentryx, did appear to have slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year.

Technical Implementation: The effect of the drug, said one, “is just not well verified by this study.” At the same time, many patients, and some physicians, saw in the data a potentially helpful medication, one that might lessen patients’ reliance on steroids, which are highly effective but often cause severe side effects.

stories.headline: Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design
stories.summary: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON OCTOBER 28, 2026 TO ML APPLICATIONS, PRODUCTION ENGINEERING Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design By Haiyu Lu, Shuo Gu, Yang Yang (Tony), Jingwen Ren, Tianchen Ji, Qing Zhang, Wentian Guo, Haocheng Wu, Siqi Zeng, Yunchen Pu, Liang Wang, Chonglin Sun This post describes the next generation of Meta Andromeda, Meta’s personalized ads retrieval engine, and how co-designing the model, system, and GPU hardware unlocks a new efficiency frontier for ads retrieval. In production, the system scores every eligible ad with near ranking-level model performance at retrieval scale and surfaces the top candidates at over one billion ads per second, a new throughput benchmark for ads retrieval-stage models (i.e., a 100x lift compared to the 2024 Meta Andromeda system).
stories.why_it_matters: For advertisers, this means better performance automatically from the retrieval system matching ads across a larger candidate pool, within the same latency budget. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.

stories.headline: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing
stories.summary: Serdar Cellat , Yuchen Xie , Bernadette Marcu , Blaid Burgess , Cody Jarrett , Carlos Pereira , Qing Shi , Samuel Carvajal , Manuel Pamplona , Dorothy Jung , Feiko Ritsema , Benjamin Klein , Alex Woo , Eugene Lok , Anna Pulido , Rebecka Swe , Sanford Holsapple , Ranjith Kumar Shetty Introduction Clips in the Netflix mobile app. At Netflix, a crucial part of our mission is ensuring our content looks stunning on any device.
stories.why_it_matters: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Traditionally, creating vertical assets meant editors and producers manually reframed horizontal videos in editing tools, a process that doesn’t scale as our catalog and use cases grow.

Technical Implementation: To support both our in‑app feed and external marketing campaigns at scale, we built an automated multi‑ratio video cropping system, tightly integrated into our internal production tools, that can generate high‑quality vertical and other aspect‑ratio variants with minimal manual effort.

Deployment & Impact: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app.

stories.headline: French lawmakers approve $11.2 billion internet tax based on traffic usage, costs $0.06 per gigabyte of content accessed
stories.summary: France has approved a proposed tax that aims to tax the amount of internet data per gigabyte sent to French users in the country, with major companies like Google, Netflix, TikTok, and Meta now in the crosshairs. According to minutes released by the National Assembly, members voted 11-10 in support of the motion on October 30 — which now means the new law has been added to the country’s next budget, despite major opposition from the government side and the finance committee rapporteur.
stories.why_it_matters: The latest amendment, introduced by socialist lawmaker Laurent Lhardit, could see content providers pay €0.055 (roughly $0.06) to the government for every gigabyte of content distributed to French users. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.

stories.headline: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
stories.summary: Advertisement Advertisement Skip to content Home About the Author Advertising/Speaking Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today October 21, 2026 7 Comments Expect to see quite a few websites serving error pages today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.
stories.why_it_matters: Image: Shutterstock.com, Sashkin. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cybersecurity.
key_points: Problem & Context: The flaws at issue are present in PHP, the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including Drupal, Magento, Joomla and WordPress.
Technical Implementation: Earlier today, PHP released an emergency security update to fix two critical bugs that can allow an attacker to execute code of their choosing on a vulnerable server.

Deployment & Impact: Cloudflare said it has already detected some exploitation of the flaw, and that at 3:02 am (UTC) it implemented web application firewall rules to protect websites from attack traffic seeking to exploit the bugs, which could cause a denial of service condition, remote code execution, and data exposure.

stories.headline: Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth
stories.summary: Google on Friday celebrated receiving a poem from its first experimental orbital AI datacenter satellite. The company's Suncatcher satellite, launched at the start of the month and put into low Earth orbit, has responded to a ground station prompt to "Write a haiku from the perspective of a TPU orbiting Earth, with the wonderful world spinning beneath you." Travis Beals, senior director of Google's interdisciplinary Paradigms of Intelligence research team, said that with Suncatcher's host and TPU trays powered up and machine learning tests completed, the onboard Gemma 4 model achieved its "Hello World" milestone by sending an inference response from orbit.
stories.why_it_matters: "During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space," wrote Beals in a blog post. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.

stories.headline: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
stories.summary: arXiv:2610.37720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory.
stories.why_it_matters: We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2610.37720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks.
Technical Implementation: We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload.
Deployment & Impact: Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B show that LRMoE reduces cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI.

stories.headline: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
stories.summary: arXiv:2610.37731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified.
stories.why_it_matters: We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2610.37731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain.
Technical Implementation: In a twin experiment with the Branin-Hoo model, we compare global and localized inference under uniform and skewed context distributions.

Deployment & Impact: An application to the k-$\epsilon$ turbulence closure in a single-column ocean model, with atmospheric surface forcing as context, shows that localized posterior calibration reduces temperature and zonal-velocity errors relative to deterministic and global-posterior calibration.
